title: 2021 AMC 10A Problem 9
statement: What is the least possible value of \((xy-1)^2+(x+y)^2\) for real numbers \(x\) and \(y?\)

solutions.text:
Expanding, we get \[ \begin{gathered} x^2y^2 - 2xy + 1 + x^2 + 2xy + y^2 \\ = x^2y^2 + x^2 + y^2 + 1. \end{gathered} \] Note that every square must be non-negative. Therefore, the minimum value is when all the terms except \(1\) are \(0,\) making the sum \(1.\)

This is attainable when \(x = y = 0.\)

Thus, D is the correct answer.
